details.description: `grok-4.20-beta-latest` is xAI's rolling alias for the newest reasoning-capable snapshot of Grok 4.20, a chat model in xAI's Grok 4 series; xAI's release notes say Grok 4.20 went live on March 10, 2026. As of xAI's model/pricing page, this alias currently resolves to the same March 9, 2026 dated snapshot served as `grok-4.20-beta-0309`, accepting text and image input and producing text output. xAI has since shipped newer Grok releases (4.3, 4.5, 4.6 and 4.7). Artificial Analysis, a third-party benchmarking site, lists the underlying snapshot as deprecated in favor of Grok 4.3, though xAI's own May 2026 model-retirement guidance does not include Grok 4.20 among the models being retired or redirected.
advantages: Supports function calling, structured outputs and extended reasoning, per xAI's published model configuration.
Artificial Analysis measured about 101 output tokens per second for the underlying snapshot, faster than the 73 token/s median it reported for comparable models.
disadvantages: Artificial Analysis lists the underlying snapshot as deprecated, recommending xAI's newer Grok 4.3 instead.
xAI's reasoning-parameter documentation lists configurable effort levels for Grok 4.5, 4.6, 4.7 and the Grok 4.20 Multi-agent model, but not for this model.
use_cases: General-purpose chat and text generation through the xAI API.
Agentic or tool-using workflows via xAI's function calling and structured outputs support.
Tasks that combine image input with text, since the model accepts both text and image input.

sources.title: Grok Model Retirement on May 15, 2026 | SpaceXAI Docs
Grok 4.20 0309 v2 - Intelligence, Performance & Price Analysis | Artificial Analysis

notes: `grok-4.20-beta-latest` is xAI's alias for the current Grok 4.20 (reasoning) snapshot; as of this research it resolves to the same March 9, 2026 snapshot as `grok-4.20-beta-0309`, per the aliases listed on xAI's model/pricing page. The catalog's 1M-token context window matches that page; Artificial Analysis's page for the underlying snapshot instead states a 2M-token context window, which I did not use. Do not confuse this with the separate `grok-4.20-multi-agent` model.
